question: What fish-related historical evidence is actually supported for Lake Tambo, and can any of it become a species or current-occurrence record?

philstar2001.supports: A historical secondary account printed common/local fish labels in a Lake Tambo travel description and called it a fishing site.
doesNotSupport: dated catch/stock event for any listed name
specific capture point within the lake
current presence, abundance, diet, or fishing advice
philstar2001.interpretation: Keep the labels as source-reported historical context only. “Maya-maya (big head carp)” is unresolved; do not map the names to scientific taxa.

pna2017.accessLimit: Direct PNA page fetch returned HTTP 403; details below are from a search-indexed article-body excerpt and remain provisional until a publisher-accessible copy is reviewed.
pna2017.additionalPlanAsReported: The indexed text mentions intended fish cages; implementation was not established.
pna2017.supports: A historical management-event discovery lead using the Lake Tambo / Sta. Juliana, Capas spelling and locality.
doesNotSupport: current fish presence or cage operation

pna2020.interpretation: The 2020 report is already reviewed as stocking context only; the common/group names do not resolve scientific identities or present wild populations.

areaClaimConflict.disposition: The 2017 indexed figure is an unresolved outlier if compared with the available regional/candidate area context. The exact waterbody matches, methods, and extents are not reconciled; do not use 25,000 ha as a confirmed lake area.
areaClaimConflict.comparisonCaveat: The BMB 2014 row is region-only with no municipality, and the OSM geometry is an unverified candidate; the records are not proven to describe the same delineation.

synthesis.fishTaxonomy: No new scientific fish taxon is validated. Historical local-name labels and generic tilapia/carp stocking labels remain unlinked to scientific species.
synthesis.wildOccurrence: Neither travel writing nor release reports establish a current wild-capture occurrence or persistence.
synthesis.geometry: The PNA 2017 area claim is not a boundary. Use the previous locality/geometry review for the BMB and OSM area caveats; geometry remains unresolved.
synthesis.publicUse: No public app species, diet, catchability, or geometry row is admitted; no source reuse approval is granted.

nextActions: Find a directly accessible PNA page or stable publisher copy for the 2017 report before relying on its details; retain the 25,000-ha figure as rejected/unverified area context.
Seek taxon-resolved fish survey reports, specimen records, or independently documented catch events at Lake Tambo with dates, methods, diagnostic basis, and exact locality.
Keep Tambo Lake and San Marcos Lake fish baselines, Central Luzon, and Luzon incomplete.

sources.supports: Full publisher page for a 2001 travel narrative mentioning Lake Tambo fishing and the printed common/local labels; no scientific or survey evidence.
Search-indexed article-body excerpt reports a 2017 release of 200,000 tilapia fingerlings in Lake Tambo, Capas; direct page retrieval returned 403.
Previously reviewed report of a 2020 stocking event; included as separate historical context, not species inventory.
Capas charter names Tambo Lake under Barangay Sta. Juliana; this is locality context only, not exact waterbody identity or boundary.
BMB approximate historical area context (91.98 ha), showing that the indexed 25,000-ha claim must not be adopted without resolution.
Previous review derives an approximate 79.37-ha community-mapped candidate; not an official boundary or reliable area measure.
